title: Make Ahead Moroccan Spiced Couscous Grain Salad
summary: This vibrant make-ahead Moroccan grain salad combines fluffy steam-cooked couscous with colorful vegetables, sweet dried fruits, and warm aromatic spices. Flaved with a zestful dressing of extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, cumin, cinnamon, and ground coriander, this grain salad actually tastes better after chilling as the ingredients meld together. Sweet orange-soaked raisins, chewy dried apricots, and crunchy toasted almonds introduce delightful texture to every forkful. Tender chickpeas provide satisfying plant-based protein while diced English cucumber and bell peppers add crisp, refreshing bite. Perfect for meal preparation, picnic lunches, or busy weekday buffets, this dish holds its texture and flavor for days in the refrigerator. Top with crumbled feta cheese, fresh mint leaves, and pomegranate arils right before serving for a stunning feast for the senses. Every bite delivers a harmonious blend of sweet, savory, and tangy North African inspired notes.

steps.step: Measure one and a half cups of dried couscous into a large heatproof glass or ceramic mixing bowl.
Bring two cups of vegetable broth to a rolling boil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add half a teaspoon of salt, turmeric powder, and one tablespoon of olive oil to the boiling broth.
Pour hot boiling vegetable broth directly over dry couscous inside heatproof glass mixing bowl.
Stir couscous once with a fork to ensure all grains are completely submerged in hot broth.
Cover glass bowl tightly with plate or plastic wrap to trap steam and let rest for ten minutes.
Measure extra virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, orange juice, and orange zest into a glass jar.
Add ground cumin, ground cinnamon, ground coriander, smoked paprika, and ground ginger to dressing jar.
Add honey, apple cider vinegar, harissa paste, garlic powder, and onion powder into glass dressing jar.
Season dressing with remaining salt and black pepper before sealing glass jar with tight lid.
Shake dressing jar vigorously for thirty seconds until oil, juice, and spices form emulsified sauce.
Rinse canned chickpeas thoroughly in colander under cold water and drain completely for five minutes.
Spread drained chickpeas onto paper towel lined baking sheet and pat dry to remove moisture.
Dice dried apricots, dried figs, English cucumber, red bell pepper, and red onion into uniform pieces.
Toast sliced almonds and pine nuts in dry skillet over medium heat for three minutes until golden.
Transfer toasted nuts onto plate immediately to stop cooking and prevent burning delicate slices.
Finely chop fresh mint leaves, flat-leaf parsley, dill, and green onions on clean cutting board.
Slice kalamata olives and pitted green olives into small thin rings for rich briny flavor notes.
Uncover steamed couscous after ten minutes rest time and inspect grains for tender fluffy texture.
Fluff steamed couscous thoroughly using large kitchen fork, separating grains completely without mash.
Allow fluffed couscous to cool at room temperature for fifteen minutes before adding fresh veggies.
Pour half of prepared spiced Moroccan dressing over warm fluffed couscous inside large glass bowl.
Toss warm couscous gently with fork so grains absorb fragrant olive oil dressing as they cool down.
Add dried apricots, golden raisins, and chopped dried figs into dressed warm couscous grain base.
Stir dried fruit gently into couscous so sweet pieces absorb warm spice flavors and plump up nicely.
Add drained chickpeas and sliced olives into couscous bowl, stirring gently to mix evenly throughout.
Add diced English cucumber, red bell pepper, and red onion to couscous mixture once cooled.
Pour remaining spiced dressing over entire grain salad bowl to coat fresh vegetables thoroughly.
Toss grain salad gently with two large serving spoons until all ingredients are evenly distributed.
Add toasted sliced almonds, pine nuts, and chopped pistachios into grain salad, reserving small portion.
Add fresh chopped mint, parsley, dill, green onions, capers, and zaatar spice into grain salad.
Toss salad again carefully to incorporate herbs without crushing delicate fresh cucumber cubes.
Taste grain salad and season with small pinch of sumac powder or salt if extra tang is desired.
Cover salad bowl tightly with lid or plastic wrap to prepare for make-ahead refrigeration step.
Refrigerate Moroccan couscous grain salad for at least two hours or overnight to meld all flavors.
Observe how couscous grains absorb savory dressing notes during chilling period in refrigerator.
Prepare crumbled feta cheese and pomegranate arils in separate glass containers for final plating.
Keep extra toasted nuts and fresh herbs in small sealed baggies to maintain crunch and color.
Remove chilled salad bowl from refrigerator fifteen minutes prior to serving to take off chill.
Fluff chilled grain salad gently with fork to separate grains that may have compacted while cold.
Drizzle one tablespoon of luxury argan oil over salad before plating for rich authentic nutty finish.
Transfer chilled make-ahead Moroccan grain salad into large decorative ceramic serving platter dish.
Scatter crumbled feta cheese evenly across top surface of couscous grain salad for rich contrast.
Sprinkle pomegranate arils over feta layer to add vibrant ruby red color and sweet juicy bursts.
Garnish with reserved toasted almonds, pistachios, pine nuts, and a light sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Decorate top of salad platter with fresh mint sprigs, lemon zest, and sumac powder for presentation.
Serve make-ahead grain salad cold or at cool room temperature as light main dish or side dish.
Pair salad with grilled flatbreads, hummus, falafel, or roasted skewers for complete meal spread.
Provide large serving spoon alongside platter so guests can scoop generous portions easily.
Inform dining guests that salad contains tree nuts, dairy feta cheese, and fragrant sesame seeds.
Enjoy dynamic blend of sweet apricots, savory spices, crunchy nuts, and fluffy couscous grains.
Store leftover grain salad in glass container in refrigerator for up to four days with great taste.
Notice how salad maintains excellent texture and bold flavor without becoming soggy or bland.
Pack leftover couscous salad into lunch containers for quick, healthy, make-ahead workday meals.
Wipe salad platter rim cleanly before serving to maintain crisp, colorful, professional look.
Keep extra dressing jar in fridge to refresh salad portions if stored for multiple days ahead.
